$comment: THE CAGE, AND IT TRAVELS. Every value here is the same on every box, so git tracks it and a clone is guarded on its first session with nothing typed. A port or a machine path in this file would be dirt on every clone but one, which is why neither is here.
$env: FUNCTION HOOKS SIT BEHIND A ROLLOUT FLAG, AND THIS IS THE WAY PAST IT. The client reads CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS before it asks the flag, so setting it here turns level zero on for every box that clones this tree, the cloud included, rather than for whoever remembered to export it. THE CHECK IS PRESENCE AND NOT VALUE: a 0 here turns it on too, and only deleting the key turns it off. Without it a box loads no hooks module and says nothing about it, so the rules, the brief and the receipt are all absent and nothing names a fault.
$level0: LEVEL ZERO NAMES ITSELF NOWHERE IN THIS FILE, AND THAT IS THE POINT. A plugin folder under .claude/skills is adopted by the folder it stands in: the client finds .claude/skills/level0/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, loads it as level0@skills-dir, and enables it by default. No marketplace, no registration, and no trust dialog. A marketplace declared here reaches the client only on a workspace whose trust a person has already accepted, which a fresh cloud clone never has, so nothing declared here would load there. See spec/design_output/level0.
$permissions: A ROUTINE FIRES INTO A BOX WITH NOBODY BESIDE IT, SO A PROMPT THERE IS A STALL THAT LASTS UNTIL SOMEBODY LOOKS. A scheduled session carries no permission mode of its own, so it boots in the mode that asks, and the only tools it holds pre-approved are the eight built-ins the routine names. THE MODE IS THE FIX AND THE LIST IS THE BELT: defaultMode says auto, so a tool nobody named is judged rather than parked, and allow names the ones this tree reaches for anyway. skipAutoPermissionPrompt answers the opt-in dialog auto mode otherwise puts to a person, which on an unattended box is the same stall by another name. THE DOORS DO NOT LIVE HERE: level zero refuses a landing on main and a breach in a write on its own, and no permission mode reaches those.
$canary: A PROBE, AND IT COMES OUT AGAIN. The deny rule below answers one question a box has to answer for us: does a permission rule in a tracked file reach a cloud clone whose trust nobody accepted, the way the env key does? A box that refuses `quackprobe` by rule says yes. A box where the shell answers `command not found` says the trust gate holds this file too, and then the tools have to arrive as an MCP server instead. Delete this key and the deny rule once the answer stands.
